thread:
anya: Heads up — noticed preview invoices showing fractional token credits after alias+fallback routing during the canary. Example: request to `text-ricos-1` got routed to `text-ricos-1-quant` and preview shows both token counts. Anyone else see this?

devon: repro'd. Looks like the route resolver emits both the original route tag and the fallback tag, and our metering pipeline currently aggregates by `req_id` but the proxy creates a new `req_id` for fallback attempts. So we end up with two distinct events.

maria: ugh. So we have (a) duplicate req_id due to proxy and (b) different model alias metadata. Quick mitigation: add `canonical_request_id` and `canonical_model` into the ingest event as soon as it hits the edge, before any fallback attempts. Then downstream dedupe can prefer canonical_request_id if present.

liam: adding fields helps but note payload blowup — downstream kafka/storage per-event size will go up. Also some consumers (legacy billing joins) assume fixed schema. We need a migration plan.

ops-eng: alternative: dedupe at the aggregator using a fingerprint of (tenant_id, session_id, prefix_kv_hash). If fingerprint matches within 1s window, coalesce counts and prefer the highest-fidelity model tag. Avoids changing many producers.

anya: both sound viable. Which is lower risk for a quick canary fix?

devon: low-risk quick fix = add `canonical_request_id` at ingress (edge proxy already knows it). Consumers can ignore until we flip a flag. Longer term do fingerprinting in aggregator as a safety net. I'll sketch both.

maria: sample event we can start emitting (edge pseudocode):

```json
{
  "req_id": "r_abc123",
  "canonical_request_id": "r_abc123_original",
  "model_alias": "text-ricos-1",
  "canonical_model": "text-ricos-1-quant",
  "tenant_id": "t-42",
  "tokens": 137
}
```

liam: good example. We'll need a consumer compatibility flag in consumer config (eg `prefers_canonical_id`) otherwise some joins will break.

ops-eng: console UX ask: show preview invoices as provisional vs settled. Provisional should be excluded from final invoice totals and show an explanatory tooltip: "Provisional: may include duplicate counts during route fallback — final invoice will reconcile." That will stop customers from panicking during rollout.

anya: +1. Can we also add a short metric: `billing.preview_dup_rate` to alert if duplicates > 0.2%?

devon: yes. I'll add a Prometheus counter at aggregator when we see deduped events and expose preview vs final diff. Canary plan: emit `canonical_request_id` for 2% of traffic for 30m, monitor `preview_dup_rate` and `invoice_preview_delta`. If <0.1% we roll to 25% then 100%.

sre-bot: deploy: ingest-edge v4.9.1 -> canary (2%) ✅

maria: I'll open the PR with schema change + consumer flag and a migration note for billing team. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8421

anya: thanks. tagging @ops-eng and @billing-team to review UX/messaging. :eyes:
